subject: Post-call: monthly burn scenarios, $/1M token targets & PO trigger checklist
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@novafarm.com>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@novafarm.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: monthly burn scenarios, $/1M token targets & PO trigger checklist

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on expected traffic. Quick recap + asks so we can align procurement and legal timelines: 

Highlights from the call:
- Pilot scope: 10k end-user actions/day on first pass (customer-facing suggestions), mostly short completions (avg ~800 tokens per request).
- Primary success metric: latency <500ms p95, cost visibility to keep pilot < $10k/month if possible.
- Regulatory: Novafarm handles PHI in a separate flow; this pilot is non-PHI but you flagged SOC2 and data retention requirements.

Immediate asks (so we can size procurement):
1) Confirm range of daily requests you want to model for pilot (you said 5k-30k/day as low/typical/high).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens for a committed pilot or preferred price band (you mentioned aiming for ~$15-25 per 1M tokens).
3) Tell us whether purchase will be via card or needs a PO (and any internal PO threshold).

I attached a short workbook that runs three scenarios (low/med/high) and maps to monthly token totals + cost at multiple $/1M points. Below is the math we covered on the call so there is no ambiguity: 

Scenario math (same sheet in attachment):
- Low: 5,000 requests/day * 800 tokens = 4M tokens/day -> ~120M tokens/month
- Mid: 10,000 requests/day * 800 tokens = 8M tokens/day -> ~240M tokens/month
- High: 30,000 requests/day * 800 tokens = 24M tokens/day -> ~720M tokens/month
Cost examples at $/1M tokens:
- $15/1M -> Low: $1,800 | Mid: $3,600 | High: $10,800
- $20/1M -> Low: $2,400 | Mid: $4,800 | High: $14,400
- $25/1M -> Low: $3,000 | Mid: $6,000 | High: $18,000

Procurement note: if your mid/high scenario puts you above your internal PO threshold, we should start PO paperwork now — Redwood can accept net-30 PO for pilots that cross the threshold, but finance lead time varies. Vanessa (cc'd) can confirm typical lead times and any accelerator options.

Next steps I propose:
- Samantha/Ben: confirm the single scenario to model for a 60-day pilot (pick low/mid/high) and indicate PO vs card by EOD Thu 6/10.
- Vanessa: confirm Redwood procurement lanes and estimated PO lead time (vanessa, can you capture in the thread?).
- I’ll put together a short pricing quote (scenario-based) and a one-page SoW for the pilot once we have scenario + billing path.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0142
Redwood Inference
Attachments: spend-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet), procurement-lanes.pdf (procurement playbook)
From: Samantha Green <samantha@novafarm.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@novafarm.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: monthly burn scenarios, $/1M token targets & PO trigger checklist

Thanks Soojin — this is very helpful. Agree with the numbers and the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed pilot modeling (internal):
- We want to model mid (10k/day) and a conservative high (30k/day) to make sure we don't under-provision.
- For the purchasing path: we prefer to pay by corporate card for the initial 60-day pilot if possible, but finance has indicated anything over ~$7.5k/month will need a PO. We can try to keep the pilot under that threshold but want a plan if we hit the high scenario.
- Target pricing: our procurement contact suggested target ~$18/1M tokens for a pilot commitment (monthly review), with flexibility down to $15 if we commit to a larger, multi-quarter plan.

A couple of items for your team:
- Can you confirm whether prefix caching or reranking will be included in the pilot pricing assumptions? That materially affects tokens/rounds per request.
- We need a short SOC2 excerpt to share with our security team (redwood's scope and evidence).

If you can confirm the procurement lanes and the caching note, we can tell finance to keep the card option open for the first invoice. I’ll check internally about pushing to a PO if we see high usage quickly (we estimate ~1 week to approve a PO once the amount is finalized).

—Sam
Director, Product Operations
Novafarm
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@novafarm.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@novafarm.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 07:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: monthly burn scenarios, $/1M token targets & PO trigger checklist

Hi team — quick procurement clarification from Redwood Ops: 

Procurement lanes (pilot guidance):
- Card (auto-bill): up to $7,500/month — fastest path, immediate provisioning.
- PO (net-30): required for recurring spend > $7,500/month. Typical finance lead time: 10–14 business days from signed SOW/quote to first invoice scheduling.
- If Novafarm expects to enter the high scenario (> $10k/month) within pilot window, we advise starting PO paperwork in parallel and use the card for the first invoice to avoid a gap.

Caching note: prefix/KV caching and basic reranking are supported in the pilot by default — Redwood will not double-charge tokens for cached prefixes when the cache hit rate is >80% in production-like traffic. Our quote will include an assumed cache hit of 45% for the first 30 days unless you provide traffic replay logs. If you can share request samples, we can run a cache-sensitivity projection (I included a tab in spend-scenarios.xlsx).

Attachments included in this reply: procurement-lanes.pdf (procurement matrix + contact list), SOC2-excerpt.pdf (summary & scope).

Vanessa Ortiz
Finance & Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha@novafarm.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Ben Ortiz <ben.ortiz@novafarm.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: monthly burn scenarios, $/1M token targets & PO trigger checklist

Appreciate the fast responses — summary and next steps below (so nothing falls through):

Summary of scenarios (attached workbook has live formulas):
- Low (5k/day): 120M tokens/mo • Cost @ $18/1M = $2,160/mo
- Mid (10k/day): 240M tokens/mo • Cost @ $18/1M = $4,320/mo
- High (30k/day): 720M tokens/mo • Cost @ $18/1M = $12,960/mo

Procurement gating (as Vanessa noted):
- If Novafarm stays at mid or below, card billing is a viable path (mid =~ $4.3k @ $18/1M).
- If you land in high scenario, please start PO paperwork now — estimated PO lead time = 10–14 business days. We will accept card for the first invoice and apply credit to PO invoice once processed.

Action items / timeline:
- [Samantha] Confirm which scenario you want us to price and whether you want the quote based on $15 / $18 / $20 per 1M tokens by Friday 6/11.
- [Samantha/Ben] Share a small traffic sample (anonymized) if you want us to run cache-hit projections (drive link above).
- [Vanessa] I’ll expect an outline of the PO contact info and any non-standard terms; we’ll route to legal if needed.

I’ll send a scenario-based quote and one-page SOW once we have the scenario and billing path. Thanks — planning to book a 15-min alignment call next week if that helps (suggest Mon 6/14 morning PT).

Best,
Soojin
